description: The goal of the course is to give students the background and skills of medical image computing.

syllabus.title: Introduction to Medical Imaging
syllabus.body: Basic image processing techniques, noise and error propagation and methods to handle it, medical image enhancement, introduction to medical imaging modalities and image analysis software.

syllabus.title: Image Registration and Segmentation
syllabus.body: Rigid and non-rigid registration models with demonstration, texture in medical images, medical image segmentation: region growing and clustering, random walks, active contours, systematic evaluation and validation, decision trees, random forests, and neural networks for segmentation and classification.

syllabus.title: Image Analysis
syllabus.body: Analysis of speckle images: ultrasound, Doppler and tissue harmonic, speckle reduction, beam steering, image compounding and filtering, cardiovascular and ophthalmic imaging, learning based and deep learning based image analysis.

syllabus.title: Applications
syllabus.body: Retinal vessel segmentation and classification, vessel segmentation in CT scan of lungs, lesion segmentation in brain MRI, tissue characterization in ultrasound, learning based diagnosis: classification and diagnosis of brain tumor, lung cancer, retinal disease, cardiovascular disease and other diseases.

outcomes: Develop skills that are vital to medical image-based diagnosis.
Have fundamental skills and understanding of medical image modalities and basic processing approaches.
Have segmentation, analysis and learning based diagnosis approach.
textbooks: G. R. Sinha, Bhagwati Charan Patel, Medical Image Processing Concepts and Applications, PHI, 2014.
Rasmus R. Paulsen, Thomas B. Moeslund, Introduction to Medical Image Analysis, Springer, 2020.
S. Kevin Zhou, Hayit Greenspan, Dinggang Shen, Deep Learning for Medical Image Analysis, Academic Press, 2017.
referenceBooks: Geoff Dougherty, Digital Image Processing for Medical Applications, Cambridge University Press, 2010.
